children: Anthropic, the artificial intelligence startup, is in talks to secure a $15 billion credit facility, just short of a much-anticipated initial public offering.

Morgan Stanley is handling the financing, with Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup also involved in a big way, sources familiar with the situation said. The same four banks are said to be leading the IPO. What catches the eye is the magnitude of the facility.

Anthropic, earlier, had an aim of around $10 billion and last year had a $2.5 billion five-year revolver. A rise to $15 billion would provide the developer of the Claude model much more financial leeway as the cost of training and serving sophisticated AI models increases.

Anthropic has also been ramping up its infrastructure obligations as demand develops. It is projected to have yearly revenue of over $65 billion, increasing substantially from the end of previous year.
The blend of fast revenue growth, steep computing spending and a significantly bigger credit line offers investors a preview of the size Anthropic might take to public markets.

The business allegedly wants to raise as much, if not more, than SpaceX did in its IPO. Next up is Anthropic's public filing to go public, which should give the clearest perspective yet of its revenue growth, cash burn and infrastructure liabilities.

title: Anthropic's IPO Push Just Got a $15 Billion Backstop
